title.narrative: BREAK FREE FAWE KENYA

description.narrative: The Break Free! consortium goes with the strategic objective that adolescents exercise their right to live free from teenage pregnancy (TP) and child marriage (CM) supported by civil society. Civil society organizations, youth-led groups and networks will be strengthened to lobby and advocate for improved legislation and implementation to increase girls’ agency and to promote social norm change in favor of the prevention of CM/TP. Three pathways of change have been identified leading towardsthe strategic programme objective: ❖ Pathway 1: Adolescent girls at risk of CM/TP access quality and safe education❖ Pathway 2: Duty bearers and decision-makers develop, resource and implement laws and policies that respond to adolescents’ needs❖ Pathway 3: Adolescents access quality SRHR information, education and servicesTo achieve these outcomes, seven key strategies have been prioritized:1. Social movement/network building2. Capacity building of (youth) civil society organizations (CSOs)3. Network building of (youth) CSOs/NGOs4. Promote access to lobby platforms5. Lobby and advocacy campaigns6. Research7. Learning and exchangeThe geographical focus of the programme is West Africa (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger), East Africa (Ethiopia, Kenya Sudan) and Southern Africa (Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia). There will also be a programming component at Africa regional level, targeting institutions and other stakeholders operating at this broader level.

The youth-led Community Based Organizations have introduced innovative ways of reaching a bigger audience, i.e. in Tana River, talent warriors are using theatre arts for sensitization in the villages and schools and this attracts more audience. Collaborative efforts with government departments and other CSOs have increased in all the counties i.e. in Kajiado where there are many CSOs and have been willing to collaborate and network, they have been inviting Break Free! for sessions during their activities and hence the increased reach and also during the commemoration of the international Days including Zero Tolerance to FGM, Menstrual Hygiene Management Day, Day of African Child (DAC), International Day of the Girl Child. Malkia’s youth were able to cascade information with other young people who also attended the events. Adolescents were also reached through dissemination of adolescent guides, school mentorship sessions , youths engaged in the consortium UPR activity and youths who attended the ICPD30 and AYSRHR scientific conference and 16 Days of Activism.

None youth led CSOs (15 - 25 years old) who report having strengthened lobby & advocacy capacities

Youth led CBOs have been trained on the Young Citizens Score Carding tool, to be able to conduct advocacy through social audit and using the tool to advocate for services. The youth-led groups were trained on Gender Transformative Programing to be gender responsive as they implement their activities. After the 2 Trainings the youth have cascaded the training to the other youth members of the CBOs. The score carding tool has been used especially in Tharaka to hold duty bearers accountable in the budgeting process to advocate for resource allocation for youth empowerment activities. After the gender training, youth are incorporating the 6 key elements of gender in their activities (working with both boys, young men and men to embrace positive masculinity, increase agency for girls and young women, working with boys, girls, including men and women in all their diversity, enabling environment where stakeholders support children and youth towards gender equality).
